# This MiniCluster manifest is designed to run the AMG2023 benchmark on an AWS EFA-enabled ARM-based Kubernetes cluster.
# It is configured for a small-scale test run on a single node, which can be scaled up by increasing the 'size' parameter.
apiVersion: flux-framework.org/v1alpha2
kind: MiniCluster
metadata:
  # Name of the MiniCluster instance
  name: amg-test-cpu-multinode
  # Target namespace for deployment
  namespace: default
spec:
  # The number of pods in the MiniCluster. Set to 1 for initial testing as requested.
  # To run across multiple nodes, increase this value (e.g., to 4).
  size: 1

  # The total number of MPI tasks (ranks) to run.
  tasks: 4

  # Keep pods running after the main command completes to allow for inspection.
  interactive: true

  # Do not delete pods after the job completes to allow for log and state inspection.
  cleanup: false

  # Flux Operator logging settings
  logging:
    # Fail the job if there are any Flux-related startup errors.
    strict: true

  # Flux-specific configuration
  flux:
    # Specify the architecture as ARM, required for ARM-based AWS instances.
    arch: "arm"
    container:
      # Use the ARM-compatible Flux view image for the sidecar.
      image: ghcr.io/converged-computing/flux-view-rocky:arm-9

  # Pod specification for scheduling on specific hardware
  pod:
    resources:
      # Request and limit AWS EFA network interfaces for high-performance networking.
      # This ensures the pod is scheduled on a node with an available EFA device.
      limits:
        vpc.amazonaws.com/efa: 1
      requests:
        vpc.amazonaws.com/efa: 1

  # Defines the application container to be run under Flux
  containers:
    - image: ghcr.io/converged-computing/fractale-agent-experiments:amg2023
      # The command to be executed by Flux.
      # Runs the AMG benchmark with problem type 2 on a small 4x4x4 grid.
      command: testamg -problem 2 -n 4 4 4
      # The launcher flag must be false; the Flux Operator injects the correct entrypoint.
      launcher: false

# This manifest corrects a previous OOMKilled failure by scaling the job down for a single-node test run.
# The changes align with the debugging instructions to start small and incrementally scale.
apiVersion: flux-framework.org/v1alpha2
kind: MiniCluster
metadata:
  name: amg-test-cpu-multinode-final
  namespace: default
spec:
  # FIX: Reduced size from 4 to 1 to adhere to the "MUST use only 1 node to first test" constraint.
  size: 1
  # FIX: Reduced tasks from 256 to 64 to match the vCPU count of a single m7g.16xlarge node and prevent oversubscription.
  tasks: 64

  # Do not delete pods after the job completes to allow for log and state inspection.
  cleanup: false
  # The number of retries before considering a job failed.
  backoffLimit: 1

  # Logging is set to strict to fail fast on any Flux startup errors, as required.
  logging:
    strict: true

  # Pod specification with scheduling and restart behavior.
  pod:
    # Ensure the job does not restart on failure, to allow for inspection of failed pods.
    restartPolicy: Never
    # The nodeSelector correctly targets the m7g.16xlarge instance type.
    nodeSelector:
      node.kubernetes.io/instance-type: m7g.16xlarge

  # Flux-specific configuration for an ARM environment.
  flux:
    arch: arm
    container:
      image: ghcr.io/converged-computing/flux-view-rocky:arm-9

  # Defines the application container to be run under Flux.
  containers:
    - image: ghcr.io/converged-computing/fractale-agent-experiments:amg2023
      # FIX: Reduced problem size and adjusted processor grid for a smaller, single-node run to prevent OOM errors.
      command: amg -problem 2 -n 128 128 64 -P 8 8 1
      # The launcher flag must be false; the Flux Operator injects the correct entrypoint.
      launcher: false

      # Environment variables for performance tuning and EFA networking are maintained.
      environment:
        FI_EFA_USE_DEVICE_RDMA: "1"
        FI_PROVIDER: "efa"
        MKL_NUM_THREADS: "1"
        OMPI_MCA_btl_vader_single_copy_mechanism: "cma"
        OMP_NUM_THREADS: "1"
        OPENBLAS_NUM_THREADS: "1"

      # Resource requests and limits for AWS EFA are required for scheduling on EFA-enabled hardware.
      resources:
        limits:
          vpc.amazonaws.com/efa: "1"
        requests:
          vpc.amazonaws.com/efa: "1"

apiVersion: flux-framework.org/v1alpha2
kind: MiniCluster
metadata:
  name: amg-test-cpu-multinode-final
  namespace: default
spec:
  backoffLimit: 1
  cleanup: false
  containers:
  - command: amg -problem 2 -n 128 128 64 -P 8 8 1
    environment:
      FI_EFA_USE_DEVICE_RDMA: '1'
      FI_PROVIDER: efa
      MKL_NUM_THREADS: '1'
      OMPI_MCA_btl_vader_single_copy_mechanism: cma
      OMP_NUM_THREADS: '1'
      OPENBLAS_NUM_THREADS: '1'
    image: ghcr.io/converged-computing/fractale-agent-experiments:amg2023
    launcher: false
    resources:
      limits:
        vpc.amazonaws.com/efa: '1'
      requests:
        vpc.amazonaws.com/efa: '1'
  flux:
    arch: arm
    container:
      image: ghcr.io/converged-computing/flux-view-rocky:arm-9
  logging:
    strict: true
  pod:
    nodeSelector:
      node.kubernetes.io/instance-type: m7g.16xlarge
    restartPolicy: Never
  size: 1
  tasks: 64

manager.name: Deploy AMG2023
manager.description: Build a Docker container and deploy it as a Kubernetes Job.

context.environment: AWS CPU instance in Kubernetes to run across nodes
context.optimize:
Maximize the amg2023 figure of merit. You MUST maximize memory per CPU core. More cores are better.
You MUST run amg across UP TO 4 nodes. You MUST start with 1, then 2 nodes. You MUST set environment variables for MPI to use EFA with libfabric.
The trick to optimizing this is THREADING. You MUST force OpenMP and any math libraries to use only one thread per MPI rank. On example is setting OMP_NUM_THREADS to "1". You might also consider setting OMPI_MCA_btl_vader_single_copy_mechanism to "cma" as a conservative builder will set to none.
YOU MUST SLOWLY increase the problem size, one dimension at a time, by an increment no more than double the current to increase the FOM. A timeout may not require a smaller problem size but rather a different instance.
A previous run example that has worked well:
  amg -problem 2 -n 128 128 128 -P 8 4 1 on m7g.16xlarge with FOM 8.039496e+08
The size of the MiniCluster MUST be no larger then 4. Tasks MUST be at least 4 per node.
To reduce noise in logging, you can set logging.quiet to true.
context.resources:
The resource spec you got earlier is for an autoscaling cluster, so the nodes possible are not there. You must add the nodeSelector to use:  
  m7g.16xlarge, 64 CPU, 256 GiB Memory, ARM (Graviton3)
You are still limited to up to 4 nodes.
context.testing: You MUST run AMG -problem 2. For testing choose a small problem size no greater than 4 in any dimension.
context.details:
You MUST run on up to 4 nodes and you MUST use only 1 node to first test. 
You MUST set resource requests and limits to use vpc.amazonaws.com/efa: 1
Tasks MUST be at least 4.
You MUST NOT oversubscribe.
Since this is an ARM instance you MUST change the flux.container.image to be
ghcr.io/converged-computing/flux-view-rocky:arm-9. Otherwise, do not change or set it.
If you are using an ARM instance you MUST also set flux.arch: "arm".
